prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1345; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers were dispatched to a two-vehicle collision on a roadway in Houston, Texas, where a low-speed head-on collision had occurred. Driver 1 and Driver 2 were both present at the scene, along with one Passenger seated in Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and said the impact was brief but jarring. Driver 2 and two independent witnesses stated that the collision happened in the manner Driver 1 described, and scene photographs are consistent with those accounts. Damage to the front end of both vehicles is largely in line with the reported impact speed and angle. Officers confirmed that Driver 1 was in the vehicle at the time of the crash, and Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the applicable policy. Nothing observed at the scene or reported by those involved suggested prior damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 was evaluated at the scene and transported for further examination as a precaution.
